resources.string: Point this tablet at your Cody server. The address and credential are checked before anything is saved.
A bare host works; http:// is assumed unless you type https://.
Your password is used once to create a token for this device, then discarded.
Create one in Cody\'s account settings, then paste it here.
That is not a server address. Try a host name, or host:port.
The server rejected that token. Check that you pasted all of it, and that it has not been revoked.
This device\'s token cannot create another token. Sign in with your password instead, or paste a token made in Cody\'s settings.
This account already has the maximum number of tokens. Revoke one in Cody\'s account settings and try again.
Cannot reach that address. Check the host, the port, and that you are on the same network or tailnet.
Not found on that server. It may be a different Cody, or an older one.
Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
The server\'s answer could not be read. It may be a newer or older Cody than this app expects.
Your token is no longer valid. Connect again.
No sessions yet. Start one in Cody and it will appear here.
Pick a session to read it here.
This session has no messages yet.
This build cannot display a “%1$s” message.
The stop request did not reach the server: %1$s
The agent runs commands in this directory and can read the files under it.
This session is new. Send the first message.
Termux command runner — not an interactive shell
Nothing has been run yet. Each command is sent to Termux, runs to completion in a fresh login shell, and comes back with its output and exit code. Working directory: %1$s
Command — one shot, no shell state kept
No result after five minutes. Termux may still be running this: a command sent with RUN_COMMAND cannot be cancelled once it has started.
Termux dropped the first %1$d characters. It returns at most 100 KB of output per command, and keeps the end.
Showing the last %1$d of %2$d characters. Copy takes all of it.
Not sent. The command is %1$d KB and Termux accepts at most %2$d KB. Write it to a file in the workspace and run that file instead.
Not sent. Android will not let Cody start Termux while Cody is in the background.
Termux could not run this, and gave no reason.
Termux refused: commands from other apps are switched off.

This screen drives the Termux app; without it there is nowhere to run a command. Install Termux from F-Droid or from its GitHub releases — and then stay with that one source. Termux and its add-ons are signed per source, so mixing them fails to install with a signature error.
Termux has not been allowed to take commands from Cody

Cody needs the “Run commands in Termux environment” permission (com.termux.permission.RUN_COMMAND). Termux defines it rather than Android, so it sits under Additional permissions instead of with the usual ones.
The system will not show that dialog again. Open App info → Permissions → Additional permissions and allow “Run commands in Termux environment”.

Termux is installed and the permission is granted, and Termux still refuses. Running commands on behalf of another app stays off until it is switched on in Termux\'s own config, and off is the default every build ships with — nothing has gone wrong. Add this line to %1$s:
Then run termux-reload-settings in Termux, or restart it, and check again.
Termux is installed and permitted, but it did not run the check command. Opening Termux once, so its bootstrap finishes, fixes this more often than not.
The shared workspace does not exist yet
Termux has no access to shared storage, so %1$s could not be created and commands are running in Termux\'s home directory instead. Run this in Termux and grant the storage permission it asks for:
No lines match this filter yet.
logcat exited on its own. That almost always means the read was refused.
With Shizuku running, Cody can read this tablet\'s whole system log — every app, not only its own — so you can debug what you are building here without plugging it into a computer.
Shizuku is not installed. It hands an app ADB-level access without root, which is the only way a sideloaded app can read the device log.
Shizuku is installed but not running. Start it from the Shizuku app; without root it has to be started again after every reboot.
This copy of Shizuku is older than v11 and does not have the permission API Cody needs. Update it and come back.
Shizuku is running but has not authorised Cody yet.
Shizuku access was refused permanently, so it cannot be asked for from here any more. Re-enable Cody in Shizuku\'s own app list.
Shizuku is ready. Granting takes one tap and one restart, and the access survives Shizuku being stopped afterwards.
Cody already had device log access.
Granted. Android only applies a new permission to a new process, so Cody has to restart before the log opens.
Shizuku stopped responding before the grant went through. Check that it is still running, then try again.
This Android build would not let Cody reach the package manager, so nothing was changed. Granting by hand still works: adb shell pm grant %1$s android.permission.READ_LOGS\n\n%2$s
Android offered no package manager to grant against. Nothing was changed.
The server did not report a user for this token.
The address and the token are still stored. Nothing has to be typed again once the server answers.
Catppuccin Latte and Mocha, the two palettes Cody ships as its defaults.
This device\'s token is encrypted at rest with a hardware-backed AES-256-GCM key from the Android Keystore.
It is never displayed — not here, not anywhere. The server keeps only a digest of it, and a screen is the easiest place for a secret to be photographed.
Signing out and forgetting the token are one action: either way the credential is deleted from this tablet.
Sign out and forget the token?
Cody returns to the connect screen and the credential is deleted from this tablet. The token itself keeps working elsewhere — revoke it in Cody\'s account settings if that is what you want.
Not installed, so there is nowhere for the Terminal surface to run a command.
Installed, and Cody has not been allowed to run commands in it.
Installed and permitted, and still refusing: commands from other apps are switched off in Termux\'s own config.
Termux answered the check with an error.
Ready, but Termux has no access to shared storage, so commands run in its home directory instead of %1$s.
Not installed. It is optional: it buys on-device system logs and nothing else.
Installed but not running. Without root it has to be started again after every reboot.
Older than v11, so it does not have the permission API Cody needs.
Running, and Cody has not been authorised yet.
Access was refused permanently, so it cannot be asked for from here. Re-enable Cody in Shizuku\'s own app list.
Running and authorised. Device log access is granted from the Logs surface — one tap and one restart.
Device log access is granted. If the Logs surface still shows nothing, Cody has not been restarted since the grant.
A surface is hidden when the backend does not advertise the capability behind it. This is that list.
The server\'s capability report could not be read, so this is the core set the app assumes: sessions, streaming and prompts.
